references.text: Describes the promised land as a land flowing with milk and honey, a good land—the same promise of the good land that the Lord leads the people into.
The spies confirm that the land flows with milk and honey, demonstrating its fertility and goodness.
Describes the promised land with water springs and rain from heaven, in contrast to Egypt—the same theme of the land's abundant water supply.
Praises God for sending springs into the valleys and watering the mountains—the same image of God's blessing through water in the landscape.
The Lord promises to open rivers on the heights and springs in the valleys—the same theme of God's blessing through water in dry places.
Concerns how the Lord leads the people into the promised land with goods they did not work for themselves.
Continues the description of the good land with all its blessings and riches.
A prophetic vision of water flowing from the temple and giving life—a similar image of life-giving water in the promised land.
